title: 5 Signs a Real Estate Storm Is Coming in an Off-Plan Market
seoTitle: 5 Signs a Real Estate Storm Is Coming
description: Five warning signs that an off-plan market is in trouble, with examples from Toronto and Dubai, and why it is not the same as a crash forecast.
answer: Five signs warn that an off-plan market is heading for trouble: the buyers are mostly investors, new units cost far more than finished ones nearby, rent no longer covers the mortgage, developers soften deals instead of cutting prices, and buyers start choosing finished homes over presale. Toronto showed all five before its presale sales collapsed.
body:
You do not need to predict a crash to see one coming. Off-plan markets give clear signals well before the storm arrives. These are the five I watch.

## The five signs

1. **The line is made of investors.** When most presale buyers plan to resell or rent instead of living in the unit, demand depends on prices rising. In Toronto, investors were 70% or more of presale buyers, according to Urbanation and CIBC.
2. **New is much more expensive than finished.** If a new unit costs far more than a resale next door, the gap has to close somehow. In Toronto today, an unsold new condo costs about 60% more per square foot than a resale.
3. **Rent does not pay the mortgage.** Once rental income falls below the monthly payment, investors start losing money and stop buying.
4. **Developers soften the deal instead of cutting the price.** Incentives appear while the headline price stays the same. That is a sign the price is under pressure.
5. **Buyers choose finished homes.** When buyers prefer what they can see today, belief in off-plan is fading. In Dubai, the share of ready homes sold rose from 24% to 29% in the third quarter of 2026.

## How to use the list

One sign alone does not mean much. Several at once deserve attention. Toronto showed all five before new condo sales fell to the lowest level since 1991. Before you commit to a presale, check how many of these signs are already visible in that market.

## A warning, not a forecast

To be fair, this is not a crash call. The 2026 UBS Global Real Estate Bubble Index placed Miami and Dubai in the elevated risk category, not the highest, and Miami cooled down from the top of the list. The storm is not here yet. But if you know where to look, you can see clouds on the horizon. This is my opinion, not financial or legal advice.

The full episode explains who creates off-plan believers and what happens when they leave. Listen at [/podcast/off-plan-runs-on-believers-here-is-how-it-breaks/](/podcast/off-plan-runs-on-believers-here-is-how-it-breaks/).
takeaways: An investor-heavy buyer base makes an off-plan market fragile.
A large price gap between new and resale units is a warning sign.
When rent stops covering the mortgage, investors stop buying.
Incentives instead of price cuts and a shift to finished homes signal fading belief.
faq: How do you know a real estate market is about to drop?
Look for investors dominating demand, new units priced far above resales, rents below mortgage payments, developer incentives replacing price cuts, and buyers shifting to finished homes.
Why do developers offer incentives instead of lowering prices?
Lowering the headline price can hurt buyers who already signed. Incentives protect the listed price, which is why they often show the price is under pressure.
Ready homes gained share in 2026. As reported for the third quarter, the share of ready homes sold in Dubai rose from 24% to 29%.
